# Data dictionary

> **Demonstration data. Synthetic records, not ARDE/KUBAHO data.**

*Generated by `src/model.py` on 14 October 2026 from the warehouse (`data/warehouse/arde.duckdb`) and `config/data_dictionary.yaml`. Do not edit by hand: change the YAML file instead.*

The warehouse is a star schema: **fact** tables hold events and results; **dimension** tables describe them (what, where, when, who). Every fact row has `source_file`, `source_sheet` and `source_row`, so any number can be traced to the Excel row it came from. Rows that broke a critical data-quality rule are in `quarantine`, not in the facts. The same tables are exported to `data/exports/` as CSV and Parquet for Power BI.

No table holds names, phone numbers or national ID numbers. People and donors are identified by salted hashes (`beneficiary_key`, `donor_key`).

## Tables

| Table | Kind | Rows | Key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dim_programme` | dimension | 2 | programme_id | One row per programme. |
| `dim_project` | dimension | 5 | project_id | One row per project. Each project belongs to one programme. |
| `dim_activity` | dimension | 15 | activity_id | One row per type of activity a project runs (the activity list, not each event). |
| `dim_location` | dimension | 152 | location_id | One row per village, plus one row per district (for results reported at district level, such as monthly indicator reports). District rows have no sector, cell or village. Provinces and districts are Rwanda's real ones; sectors, cells and villages are synthetic while on demonstration data. |
| `dim_indicator` | dimension | 12 | indicator_id | One row per MEAL indicator in config/indicator_catalogue.yaml (draft, for co-design with ARDE/KUBAHO staff). |
| `dim_date` | dimension | 1,461 | date | One row per calendar day, with Rwanda's fiscal year (July to June). |
| `dim_beneficiary` | dimension | 1,509 | beneficiary_key | One row per person (after duplicate matching). No names, phone numbers or ID numbers: the person is identified only by a salted hash. Details come from the person's earliest registration that passed the data-quality checks. |
| `dim_donor` | dimension | 25 | donor_key | One row per donor. Organisations keep their names; individual donors appear only as "Individual donor #NNN". Contact names, emails and phone numbers are never stored. |
| `fact_activity` | fact | 2,727 | source_file, source_sheet, source_row | One row per activity event from the activity monitoring files and digitised paper records. Rows that broke a critical rule are not here: they are in the quarantine table. |
| `fact_beneficiary_service` | fact | 4,475 | source_file, source_sheet, source_row | One row per service a registered person received. |
| `fact_indicator_result` | fact | 586 | source_file, source_sheet, source_row | One row per indicator value reported in the monthly indicator reports (per project, district, month and, where relevant, sex). Rows that broke a critical rule are in the quarantine table instead. |
| `fact_opportunity` | fact | 26 | opportunity_id | One row per funding opportunity in the donor tracker. |
| `dq_results` | data quality | 14 | rule_id | One row per data-quality rule (config/dq_rules.yaml), with how many records it checked and how many broke it. |
| `dq_dimension_scores` | data quality | 7 | dimension | One row per data-quality dimension, plus an "overall" row (the average of the six). |
| `dq_by_source_file` | data quality | 26 | source_file, source_sheet | One row per Excel file and sheet read, with how many of its rows had problems. |
| `dq_by_field_officer` | data quality | 4 | field_officer | One row per field officer (activity records and indicator reports), with their data-quality results. |
| `quarantine` | data quality | 240 | source_file, source_sheet, source_row | Every row that broke a critical rule, with the reasons. These rows are kept here, not in the fact tables, until the source Excel file is corrected and the pipeline is run again. |
| `review_queue` | data quality | 287 | source_file, source_sheet, source_row | Every row with warnings (and no critical problem). The row is used in results, but a person should check it. |
| `skipped_sheets` | data quality | 0 | source_file, source_sheet | Every sheet the pipeline could not read, with the reason and the column headers it did not recognise. |
| `dq_info_measures` | data quality | 5 | metric | Data-quality measures shown on the dashboard instead of rows to review (info-level flags). |
| `report_completeness` | data quality | 417 | project_id, district, period | One row per monthly indicator report that was due, and whether it arrived. |

| From | To |
|---|---|
| `dim_project.programme_id` | `dim_programme.programme_id` |
| `dim_programme.funder_id` | `dim_donor.donor_key` |
| `dim_activity.project_id` | `dim_project.project_id` |
| `dim_beneficiary.location_id` | `dim_location.location_id` |
| `fact_activity.activity_id` | `dim_activity.activity_id` |
| `fact_activity.location_id` | `dim_location.location_id` |
| `fact_activity.date` | `dim_date.date` |
| `fact_beneficiary_service.beneficiary_key` | `dim_beneficiary.beneficiary_key` |
| `fact_beneficiary_service.activity_id` | `dim_activity.activity_id` |
| `fact_beneficiary_service.date` | `dim_date.date` |
| `fact_indicator_result.indicator_id` | `dim_indicator.indicator_id` |
| `fact_indicator_result.project_id` | `dim_project.project_id` |
| `fact_indicator_result.location_id` | `dim_location.location_id` |
| `fact_indicator_result.period_date` | `dim_date.date` |
| `fact_opportunity.donor_key` | `dim_donor.donor_key` |
| `report_completeness.project_id` | `dim_project.project_id` |

## `dim_programme`

One row per programme.

Rows: 2. Key: programme_id.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `programme_id` | VARCHAR | Programme code, e.g. PRG01. |
| `name` | VARCHAR | Programme name. |
| `thematic_area` | VARCHAR | WASH, Livelihoods, Agriculture or Environment. |
| `funder_id` | VARCHAR | The main funder, as a donor_key (links to dim_donor). |
| `start_date` | DATE | First day of the programme. |
| `end_date` | DATE | Last day of the programme. |
| `status` | VARCHAR | Programme status, e.g. active. |

## `dim_project`

One row per project. Each project belongs to one programme.

Rows: 5. Key: project_id.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | VARCHAR | Project code, e.g. PRJ01. |
| `programme_id` | VARCHAR | The programme it belongs to (links to dim_programme). |
| `name` | VARCHAR | Project name. |
| `budget_rwf` | BIGINT | Total project budget in Rwandan francs. |
| `start_date` | DATE | First day of the project. |
| `end_date` | DATE | Last day of the project. |

## `dim_activity`

One row per type of activity a project runs (the activity list, not each event).

Rows: 15. Key: activity_id.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `activity_id` | VARCHAR | Activity code, e.g. ACT01. |
| `project_id` | VARCHAR | The project that runs it (links to dim_project). |
| `activity_name` | VARCHAR | Activity name as in the activity list. |
| `activity_type` | VARCHAR | construction, training, awareness, distribution, meeting or demonstration. |

## `dim_location`

One row per village, plus one row per district (for results reported at district level, such as monthly indicator reports). District rows have no sector, cell or village. Provinces and districts are Rwanda's real ones; sectors, cells and villages are synthetic while on demonstration data.

Rows: 152. Key: location_id.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `location_id` | VARCHAR | Location code. LOC0001-style codes are villages; DIST-<district> codes are whole districts. |
| `province` | VARCHAR | Province (Kigali City, Northern, Southern, Eastern, Western). |
| `district` | VARCHAR | District (one of the 30). |
| `sector` | VARCHAR | Sector (empty for a district row). |
| `cell` | VARCHAR | Cell (empty for a district row). |
| `village` | VARCHAR | Village (empty for a district row). |

## `dim_indicator`

One row per MEAL indicator in config/indicator_catalogue.yaml (draft, for co-design with ARDE/KUBAHO staff).

Rows: 12. Key: indicator_id.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `indicator_id` | BIGINT | Number given to the indicator in the warehouse. |
| `code` | VARCHAR | Indicator code, e.g. WASH-01. |
| `name` | VARCHAR | Indicator name. |
| `level` | VARCHAR | output or outcome. |
| `unit` | VARCHAR | number, percent, hectares or RWF. |
| `higher_is_better` | BOOLEAN | True if a higher value is good (the direction of the indicator). |
| `disaggregation` | VARCHAR | How results are broken down (none or sex). |
| `frequency` | VARCHAR | monthly, quarterly, semi-annual or annual. |
| `owner` | INTEGER | Who is responsible for the indicator (to be completed in Phase 4). |
| `data_source` | VARCHAR | Where the value comes from (report or computed; detail in Phase 4). |

## `dim_beneficiary`

One row per person (after duplicate matching). No names, phone numbers or ID numbers: the person is identified only by a salted hash. Details come from the person's earliest registration that passed the data-quality checks.

Rows: 1,509. Key: beneficiary_key.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `beneficiary_key` | VARCHAR | Pseudonymous person key (salted hash). The same for every registration of one person. |
| `sex` | VARCHAR | female or male (empty if never recorded clearly). |
| `age_band` | VARCHAR | Age at registration, in bands (e.g. 25-34). |
| `household_size` | BIGINT | Number of people in the household. |
| `disability_flag` | BOOLEAN | True if the person reported a disability. |
| `location_id` | VARCHAR | Village where the person registered (links to dim_location). |

## `dim_donor`

One row per donor. Organisations keep their names; individual donors appear only as "Individual donor #NNN". Contact names, emails and phone numbers are never stored.

Rows: 25. Key: donor_key.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `donor_key` | VARCHAR | Pseudonymous donor key (salted hash). |
| `donor_name` | VARCHAR | Organisation name, or "Individual donor |
| `donor_type` | VARCHAR | bilateral, multilateral, foundation, government, private or individual. |
| `country` | VARCHAR | Donor's country. |
| `thematic_interests` | VARCHAR | What the donor funds, e.g. "WASH; Livelihoods". |

## `fact_activity`

One row per activity event from the activity monitoring files and digitised paper records. Rows that broke a critical rule are not here: they are in the quarantine table.

Rows: 2,727. Key: source_file, source_sheet, source_row.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `activity_id` | VARCHAR | Which activity (links to dim_activity). |
| `location_id` | VARCHAR | Village where it took place (links to dim_location). |
| `date` | DATE | Day it took place (empty if cancelled or not yet done; links to dim_date). |
| `participants_total` | BIGINT | Number of participants. |
| `participants_female` | BIGINT | Number of women and girls. |
| `participants_male` | BIGINT | Number of men and boys. |
| `cost_rwf` | DOUBLE | Cost in Rwandan francs. |
| `planned_date` | DATE | Day it was planned for. |
| `entry_date` | DATE | Day it was typed into Excel. |
| `status` | VARCHAR | planned, completed, delayed or cancelled. |
| `source_file` | VARCHAR | Excel file the row came from. |
| `source_sheet` | VARCHAR | Sheet in that file. |
| `source_row` | BIGINT | Row number in that sheet, as shown in Excel. |

## `fact_indicator_result`

One row per indicator value reported in the monthly indicator reports (per project, district, month and, where relevant, sex). Rows that broke a critical rule are in the quarantine table instead.

Rows: 586. Key: source_file, source_sheet, source_row.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `indicator_id` | BIGINT | Which indicator (links to dim_indicator). |

| `owner` | VARCHAR | Staff code of the person responsible. |
| `next_action` | VARCHAR | What has to happen next. |
| `next_action_date` | DATE | When the next action is due. |
| `source_file` | VARCHAR | Excel file the row came from. |
| `source_sheet` | VARCHAR | Sheet in that file. |
| `source_row` | BIGINT | Row number in that sheet, as shown in Excel. |

## `dq_results`

One row per data-quality rule (config/dq_rules.yaml), with how many records it checked and how many broke it.

Rows: 14. Key: rule_id.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `rule_id` | VARCHAR | Rule code, e.g. COM-02. |
| `dimension` | VARCHAR | completeness, validity, consistency, uniqueness, timeliness or accuracy. |
| `description` | VARCHAR | The rule in plain English. |
| `records_checked` | BIGINT | Number of records (or sheets, or expected reports) the rule applies to. |
| `records_failed` | BIGINT | Number that broke the rule. |
| `score` | DOUBLE | Percentage that passed (0 to 100). |
| `critical_failures` | BIGINT | Failures that quarantined a row. |
| `warning_failures` | BIGINT | Failures that sent a row to the review queue. |
| `info_failures` | BIGINT | Failures that are only counted. |

## `dq_dimension_scores`

One row per data-quality dimension, plus an "overall" row (the average of the six).

Rows: 7. Key: dimension.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `dimension` | VARCHAR | Dimension name, or overall. |
| `score` | DOUBLE | Average of the dimension's rule scores (0 to 100). |
| `rules` | BIGINT | Number of rules in the dimension. |

## `dq_by_source_file`

One row per Excel file and sheet read, with how many of its rows had problems.

Rows: 26. Key: source_file, source_sheet.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `source_file` | VARCHAR | Excel file. |
| `source_sheet` | VARCHAR | Sheet in that file. |
| `entity` | VARCHAR | Kind of record (activity, registration, ...). |
| `field_officer` | VARCHAR | Officer code for the file, where one officer owns it. |
| `rows_read` | BIGINT | Rows read after removing blank, title and totals rows. |
| `rows_quarantined` | BIGINT | Rows with a critical problem. |
| `rows_for_review` | BIGINT | Rows with warnings only. |
| `rows_clean` | BIGINT | Rows with neither. |
| `score` | DOUBLE | Percentage of rows read with no critical or warning problem. |
| `skipped` | BOOLEAN | True if the sheet could not be read at all. |

## `dq_by_field_officer`

One row per field officer (activity records and indicator reports), with their data-quality results.

Rows: 4. Key: field_officer.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `field_officer` | VARCHAR | Officer code. |
| `rows` | BIGINT | Rows recorded by the officer. |
| `rows_quarantined` | BIGINT | Rows with a critical problem. |
| `rows_for_review` | BIGINT | Rows with warnings only. |
| `late_entries` | BIGINT | Activity rows entered after the allowed number of days. |
| `score` | DOUBLE | Percentage of rows with no critical or warning problem. |

## `quarantine`

Every row that broke a critical rule, with the reasons. These rows are kept here, not in the fact tables, until the source Excel file is corrected and the pipeline is run again.

Rows: 240. Key: source_file, source_sheet, source_row.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `entity` | VARCHAR | Kind of record. |
| `source_file` | VARCHAR | Excel file. |
| `source_sheet` | VARCHAR | Sheet in that file. |
| `source_row` | BIGINT | Row number in that sheet, as shown in Excel. |
| `month` | VARCHAR | Month the row arrived (by entry or reporting date), if known. |
| `reasons` | VARCHAR | The critical problems, e.g. "missing_required, negative_value". |
| `details` | VARCHAR | Plain-English details of each problem. |
| `field_officer` | VARCHAR | Officer code, where known. |

## `review_queue`

Every row with warnings (and no critical problem). The row is used in results, but a person should check it.

Rows: 287. Key: source_file, source_sheet, source_row.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `entity` | VARCHAR | Kind of record. |
| `source_file` | VARCHAR | Excel file. |
| `source_sheet` | VARCHAR | Sheet in that file. |
| `source_row` | BIGINT | Row number in that sheet, as shown in Excel. |
| `month` | VARCHAR | Month the row arrived, if known. |
| `reasons` | VARCHAR | The warnings, e.g. "sum_mismatch". |
| `details` | VARCHAR | Plain-English details of each warning. |
| `field_officer` | VARCHAR | Officer code, where known. |

## `skipped_sheets`

Every sheet the pipeline could not read, with the reason and the column headers it did not recognise.

Rows: 0. Key: source_file, source_sheet.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `source_file` | INTEGER | Excel file. |
| `source_sheet` | INTEGER | Sheet in that file. |
| `entity` | INTEGER | Kind of record the sheet should hold. |
| `reason` | INTEGER | Why it was skipped. |
| `missing_required` | INTEGER | Required fields that were not found. |
| `headers_found` | INTEGER | Column headers that were not recognised. |
